explanation: Tipping in India is appreciated but entirely discretionary. In July 2022 the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) explicitly barred restaurants from adding a 'service charge' automatically or by default, and in March 2025 the Delhi High Court upheld those guidelines, ruling that service charges and tips are voluntary payments that cannot be made mandatory. Many bills still show a suggested service charge line, but customers are legally entitled to have it removed and tip separately (or not) instead.
local_tip: If a 'service charge' is already on your bill, you can ask to have it removed since it's optional by law — then leave roughly 5-10% in cash if the service was good.
regional_note: Tipping is more customary in upscale or tourist-heavy restaurants in big cities like Mumbai and Delhi than in small local eateries, where it is rare.

also_check.note: Tipping is considered insulting as it implies the staff needs extra money; excellent service is the norm.
Tipping 15-20% at restaurants is a strong social expectation since many service workers rely on tips for income.
A service charge is included in the bill (service compris) by law, so extra tipping is optional, though rounding up is appreciated.

sources.title: Delhi HC rules restaurants can't impose mandatory service charge in bills
